first_impression.reaction: Didn't expect this. 'Others are simply often told, and we say so.' A wedding site that tells me which bits are sourced and which are hearsay is rare. I jumped to the FAQ and the legal section first, as I always do, then went back and skimmed the rest.

journey.quote: Some details are recorded by a royal palace, a university journal or UNESCO. Others are simply often told, and we say so.
journey.reaction: Good. That's the honesty I look for. Tells me they know the difference between a source and a story.

journey.section: The Javanese wedding, step by step
journey.quote: Read it as the palace's account of a court ceremony, simplified over time, rather than a rulebook for every Javanese family.
journey.reaction: Upfront about the limits of the source. Nobody's pretending this is universal.

journey.quote: Siraman falls before the core rites, so elders who pour the water need to arrive a day or two early, and their flights and rooms should be planned around it.
journey.reaction: Practical, and it's a real cost line. Extra nights for elders goes straight into my spreadsheet.

journey.quote: Outside Java and Bali, the customs below are drawn from journal abstracts and a student thesis, each studying particular communities.
journey.reaction: Admitting the evidence is thin here is the right call. I'd rather know it's a student thesis than be told it's gospel.

journey.section: Can Australians marry legally in Bali?
journey.quote: This section reflects official guidance as at November 2026. It is general information, not legal advice, and rules can vary by province.
journey.reaction: Date, source, disclaimer. Exactly what I want. The embassy and Smartraveller links mean I can check it myself, which I will.

journey.section: Can Australians marry legally in Bali?
journey.quote: On the Embassy's guidance, a ceremony that is not registered is not a legal marriage, so treat a blessing on its own as a celebration only.
journey.reaction: This is the catch I'd want flagged, and they flagged it themselves instead of burying it. Big plus.

journey.section: Can Australians marry legally in Bali?
journey.quote: Same-sex marriage, fees and document details are not set out on the pages we read. Check with the embassy and the registry, including any fees, before you set a date.
journey.reaction: Saying what they don't know. Fine by me. Would still have liked a rough idea of government fees, but I understand why it's not there.

journey.section: Can Australians marry legally in Bali?
journey.quote: a Wedded Advisor can be your single point of contact for the rest of the plan, with the fee and inclusions agreed in writing before you commit.
journey.reaction: 'Agreed in writing' is better than nothing. But what's the fee model? Flat fee, percentage, or do you take a cut from the venue? That's the question that decides whether I call.

journey.quote: Whether you are honouring a partner's family or simply drawn to Bali, the best wedding there starts with the right questions.
journey.reaction: After a page of sourced facts, the ending turns soft. 'The best wedding' and 'ready to listen' is the sort of line I skip.

unanswered_questions: How is the Wedded Advisor paid: flat fee, percentage of budget, or commission from venues and suppliers?
Are supplier prices passed through at cost, or is there a mark-up?
Have you actually run an Indonesian or Bali wedding that combined a traditional rite with legal registration? A real example with the budget would help.
Does the Advisor help coordinate the CNI and Civil Registry paperwork, or is that entirely on us?

turn_offs_found.quote: When you would like to talk it through, a Wedded Advisor is ready to listen, and our [destination wedding packages](/destination-wedding-packages) show where else that conversation can lead.
turn_offs_found.why: Soft, emotional sign-off after a page of facts. Tells me nothing about what I'd be paying for. Minor, but it's the one part that reads like marketing.

would_share_with: My fiancee, for the legal section
A mate marrying into a Javanese family

cta_reaction.quote: When you are ready, [speak with a Wedded Advisor](/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=indonesian-wedding-traditions&utm_content=secondary).
cta_reaction.why: The CTA comes after the evidence, not before, and the article earned some credibility. I'd click through to see the fee model. If the next page doesn't explain how they're paid, I'm out.

top_3_changes: Swap the closing line 'the best wedding there starts with the right questions' for something concrete, like what a first call covers and what it costs (nothing, or something).
Next to 'fee and inclusions agreed in writing', add one plain sentence on how the Advisor is paid, or link to a page that says so.
Add one more FAQ: 'Can a planner handle the CNI and registry paperwork for us?' and answer honestly what you do and don't do.
